abi.signature: int readSkeletonData_pathMixTimeline(Json* timelineNode, int32_t path_constraint_index, void* animation_raw)
abi.timelineNode: B13's r4: the path sub-timeline Json node. Reads +0x1c name (0x28e8ec), +0x0c declared frame count (0x28e900 and again 0x28e9cc), +0x04 child frame list (0x28e908).
abi.path_constraint_index: models the shared stack cell [sp+0x2c] that B13's pointer scan wrote (0x28df2c). B17 reads it once at 0x28e914 and stores it at timeline+0x14 (0x28e918). B17 never writes the cell; a scan miss therefore hands over the previous constraint's index unchanged.
abi.animation_raw: spAnimation* (B13's r11). The tail reads +0x04 duration, +0x08 timelineCount, +0x0c timelines and writes all three. There is NO spSkeletonData and NO spSkeletonJson argument for this block.
abi.return: MIX_TL_SKIPPED 0 (0x28e8fc beq 0x28e048: name == "mix") or MIX_TL_PUBLISHED 1 (0x28ea0c b 0x28e048). Both original exits go to the same node-advance instruction; the code only makes the two paths observable.

functions.entry_state: r4 = timelineNode, r6 = timelineNode->name, r11 = animation, [sp+0x2c] = B13's index cell, [sp+0x48] = "mix" spilled by B13 at 0x28ded0. The block is entered ONLY from 0x28e538 `bne 0x28e8ec` (B13's non-position/non-spacing handoff); 0x28e8e8 is `b 0x28da44`, so there is no fall-through, and no other branch in the whole 13044-byte function targets 0x28e8ec.

puzzle_resolution.question: A path sub-key named exactly "mix" skips the block that builds mix timelines. Who handles "mix"?
puzzle_resolution.answer: Nobody. The 0x28e8fc `beq` target is not another handler: it is 0x28e048 `ldr r4,[r4]` (timelineNode = timelineNode->next), the same advance that every published timeline tail falls into (0x28e04c cmp / 0x28e050 bne 0x28df3c continues B13's inner dispatch). A "mix" node therefore creates nothing, reads no frames, calls no readCurve, publishes nothing, does not extend duration and reports no error. The inverse is the sharper half: every OTHER unresolved name ("rotate", "bogus", a typo, ...) falls through and IS loaded as a mix timeline.
instruction_evidence: 0x28e8ec mov r0,r6 / 0x28e8f0 ldr r1,[sp,#0x48] / 0x28e8f4 bl strcmp / 0x28e8f8 cmp r0,#0 / 0x28e8fc beq 0x28e048
0x28e048 ldr r4,[r4] / 0x28e04c cmp r4,#0 / 0x28e050 bne 0x28df3c (B13 inner loop head)
0x28e538 bne 0x28e8ec is the only B17 entry; B13 compares only "position" (0x28df48) and "spacing" (0x28e530), never "mix"
0x28e900..0x28ea0c: no second name test, no error block, no lookup
puzzle_resolution.source_intent_hypothesis: The compiled guard is literally `if (strcmp(name,"mix") == 0) goto next;` — the body runs when the name is NOT "mix", which a missing `== 0` at source level would explain. Recorded as a hypothesis about intent, not as bytecode evidence; the instruction-level conclusion does not depend on it.
puzzle_resolution.runtime_observables: fixture tests mix_name_skipped (skip direction), other_name_creates_mix (fall-through direction), mix_between_others (both orders in one path node) and skip_is_transparent (no cursor slot, no duration contribution).

functions.key_decode_correction: There is NO +4 suffix pointer. Pool 0x28eb14 is resolved by the add at 0x28e938 (PC base 0x28e940) to 0x357cc0, the START of "rotateMix", shared with B12's transform family (0x28dcd8, pool 0x28ea9c, same VA). The earlier c/spine_read_tl_path checker passed 0x28e93c as the add site — that instruction is `str r1,[sp,#0x30]` — and consequently recorded a phantom "teMix" at 0x357cc4. This module's checker pins the true add site and cross-resolves the B12 site to the same VA.

setframe_abi.registers: r0 = timeline, r1 = frameIndex, r2 = time bits, r3 = rotateMix bits, [sp] = translateMix bits (5th AAPCS word; 0x28e998 str r0,[sp])
setframe_abi.store_shape: 0x283080 add r1,r1,r1,lsl#1 (i*3); 0x283094 &frames[i*3]; 0x28309c str r2,[r1] -> frames[i*3+0] = time; 0x2830a4 str r3,[r0] -> frames[i*3+1] = rotateMix; 0x2830a0 str r4,[r0,#0x4] -> frames[i*3+2] = translateMix
setframe_abi.call_target: 0x28e9a0 bl 0x283080 — the only setFrame call in B17. The position twin 0x283028 is not called; the checker's fifth compile guard proves a reconstruction that calls it cannot link.

frame_loop.curve: readCurve(frame, timeline, frameIndex) 0x28e9a4..0x28e9b0 — B17's OWN site; B13's is 0x28dff4

tail.publish: count = animation->timelineCount (0x28e9d4); animation->timelineCount = count+1 (0x28e9e0/0x28e9e4); timelines[count] = timeline (0x28e9ec)
tail.frame_stride: THREE floats: 0x28e9dc sub r2,r2,#1 ; 0x28e9e8 add r2,r2,r2,lsl#1 ; 0x28e9f4 lsl#2 -> frames[(declared-1)*3]
tail.duration: duration = animation->duration (0x28e9d0); last = frames[(declared-1)*3] (0x28e9f8); if duration > last then last = duration (0x28e9fc vcmpe / 0x28ea04 vmovgt); animation->duration = last (0x28ea08); b 0x28e048
tail.declared_vs_child: the loop follows the child list; create (0x28e900) and the duration index (0x28e9cc) both use the declared count from Json+0x0c, so declared=3 with one child still creates 3*3 floats and reads frames[6] (never written, 0)

quirks: 0x28e918 stores the index BEFORE the frame-list NULL test at 0x28e91c; a frame-less mix timeline still gets the cell value, unlike any create-time-only field.
A name of exactly "mix" is the ONLY string this block rejects; every other name creates a mix timeline. The guard's polarity is the puzzle.

The duration is read from the LAST frame's time slot (frames[(declared-1)*3]), never from rotateMix/translateMix. A stride-2 misread would pick frames[2] (the first frame's translateMix) — the duration_stride_three fixture makes that value 9.0 on purpose.
The frames array uses the DECLARED count even when the child list is shorter; declared == 0 wraps the index to frames[-3] in 32-bit arithmetic (not driven by the fixture).
Both exits (skip and publish) target the same instruction 0x28e048; there is no error path and no success/failure distinction in the original. The two return codes are a reconstruction artefact.
The three loop keys are materialised inside the frame-present path only (0x28e920..0x28e944 are after the 0x28e91c beq), so a frame-less node never even loads the key literals.

open: Whether any shipped skeleton has a path sub-key named exactly "mix" (silently ignored) or uses another name for its mix timeline cannot be checked: no spine JSON exists in this tree.
The source-level intent behind the inverted-looking guard (likely a missing `== 0`) is not provable from bytecode alone; the compiled behaviour is pinned.
declared == 0 with a non-empty frame list wraps the duration index to frames[-3]; the fixture does not drive that malformed input (same restriction as the ik/path modules).
create with declared count 0 calls the real _spBaseTimeline_create(count*3=0) and the fixture substitutes a minimum one-frame allocation; the original's zero-size calloc behaviour is not driven.
The vtable object at +0x04 and the curves array at +0x08 are not read by B17; their exact dispose/apply semantics remain owned by the timeline type and c/spine_skeleton_data.
